name: Maine

creditorClaims.text: The published notice requires claims within 4 months after first publication (18-C M.R.S. § 3-801(1)); pre-death claims are barred at the earlier of 9 months after death or the notice periods of § 3-801 (18-C M.R.S. § 3-803(1)).

earliestClose.text: Outside supervised administration, the personal representative may close the estate by verified statement no earlier than 6 months after original appointment, after the claims period has expired (18-C M.R.S. § 3-1003(1)).

smallEstate.text: Collection by affidavit 30 days after death when the entire estate, less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $40,000 adjusted for inflation (18-C M.R.S. § 3-1201(1)(A), as amended by PL 2025, c. 76). Under § 1-108 the $40,000 is increased by the change in the annual CPI-U from 2017 to the year before death, rounded down to $100: for deaths in 2026, 40,000 x (321.943 / 245.120 - 1) = 12,536.39, rounded down to 12,500, giving $52,500 (computed from the statute and BLS annual averages).

simplified.text: Summary administration when the estate does not exceed homestead allowance, exempt property, family allowance, administration costs, funeral and last-illness expenses (18-C M.R.S. § 3-1203); affidavit collection (§ 3-1201).

filingFee.text: Probate court filing fees were not read.

personalRepFee.text: A personal representative is entitled to reasonable compensation for services (18-C M.R.S. § 3-719), reviewable by the court (§ 3-721).

attorneyFee.text: No statutory schedule; the court may review the reasonableness of compensation of any attorney employed by the personal representative (18-C M.R.S. § 3-721).
